page.title: Testing
page.desc: Checking software does what it should, automatically and repeatedly: unit tests for pieces, integration tests for seams, property-based tests for laws, fuzzing for the inputs nobody imagined.
page.intro: Checking software does what it should, automatically and repeatedly: unit tests for pieces, integration tests for seams, property-based tests for laws, fuzzing for the inputs nobody imagined.

synapses.text: Many fast unit tests, fewer integration tests, few end-to-end tests; the shape keeps feedback quick.
Code that is hard to test is usually too coupled; TDD (Kent Beck) uses that pressure deliberately.
SQLite ships with test code that outweighs the engine many times over, including out-of-memory and crash tests.

children.title: Unit tests
children.desc: Small tests of one unit in isolation. The xUnit family descends from Kent Beck's SUnit for Smalltalk; JUnit (1997) made it universal.

children.title: Property-based testing
children.desc: State a law (reversing twice is identity; decode(encode(x)) == x) and let the framework generate hundreds of inputs and shrink failures. QuickCheck (Claessen and Hughes, 2000) started it.

children.title: Fuzzing
children.desc: Feeding programs random or mutated inputs to find crashes; Barton Miller coined the term in 1988, AFL (2013) made coverage-guided fuzzing mainstream, and OSS-Fuzz runs it continuously for open source.
